title: Marine netpen farming leads to infections with some unusual parasites
study_objective: To provide an overview of unusual or newly observed parasitic infections associated with salmonid fishes reared in marine netpens.
temporal_scope: Examples drawn from observations reported up to 2000; discussion includes recent industry expansion.
focal_factor_detail: marine netpen rearing conditions and associated unusual parasite infections
comparison_detail: The article discusses differences between netpen-reared and wild/freshwater-reared salmonids in the context of parasite occurrence, but does not present a formal comparative study design.
study_outcome_detail: Occurrence and types of unusual parasitic infections in netpen-reared salmonids
evidence_passage: The article describes unusual parasite infections associated with salmonids reared in marine netpens and provides examples by host, parasite and geographic setting.

title: Blood Protein Levels of Rainbow Trout Oncorhynchus mykiss (Walbaum, 1792) Cultured in The Cage
study_system_detail: rainbow trout cultured in cages in Keban Dam Lake
study_objective: To examine monthly changes in blood protein levels of rainbow trout cultured in cages and relationships with fish length and weight.
facility_detail: cages established on Keban Dam Lake
focal_factor_detail: month/seasonal variation under cage culture conditions
comparison_detail: Monthly and seasonal differences in total protein, albumin, globulin and fibrinogen; relationships with fish length and weight.
study_outcome_detail: Total protein, albumin, globulin and fibrinogen concentrations in blood serum
evidence_passage: Fish were sampled monthly for one year from cages in Keban Dam Lake; blood serum was analysed for total protein, albumin, globulin and fibrinogen, with statistically significant monthly changes reported.

title: Parasites From Fish Farms Driving Wild Salmon to Extinction
study_system_detail: wild juvenile pink salmon populations associated with salmon farms
study_objective: To report research findings linking recurrent salmon-louse infestations associated with salmon farms to declines in wild juvenile pink salmon populations.
temporal_scope: Reports research on recurrent louse infestations and population trends including the period after 2001.
focal_factor_detail: salmon louse (Lepeophtheirus salmonis) infestations associated with salmon farms
comparison_detail: Population trends before and after recurrent louse infestations are discussed, alongside comparisons of juvenile pink salmon exposure near versus away from farms.
study_outcome_detail: Wild pink salmon population abundance and projected population decline
evidence_passage: The article reports a study linking recurrent louse infestations associated with salmon farms to reduced wild pink salmon populations and discusses the projected trajectory of population decline.
